subject: radiology
title: Crazy Paving, Ground Glass Causes and Mediastinal Compartments

steps.title: Crazy paving is two patterns stacked
steps.tx: **Crazy paving** combines ground glass opacity with superimposed interlobular septal thickening, resembling irregular paving stones on high resolution CT. The ground glass fills the paving stone while thickened septa draw its borders. Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis is the examination answer, but in daily practice oedema, haemorrhage and infection produce the pattern far more often, so the clinical story must pick the cause.
steps.say: Crazy paving combines ground glass opacity with superimposed interlobular septal thickening, resembling irregular paving stones. The ground glass fills each stone while thickened septa draw its borders. Alveolar proteinosis is the examination answer, but oedema, haemorrhage and infection produce the pattern far more often in daily practice.

steps.title: Alveolar proteinosis fills alveoli with surfactant
steps.tx: **Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis** accumulates surfactant like material inside alveoli because macrophages fail to clear it, most often from antibodies against granulocyte macrophage colony stimulating factor. It favours central and symmetric lung zones while sparing apices and costophrenic angles. Patients pick up Nocardia infections, including brain abscess, and about thirty percent progress toward fibrosis. Whole lung lavage washes out the material and remains the defining treatment.
steps.say: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis accumulates surfactant like material inside alveoli because macrophages fail to clear it, most often from antibodies against a macrophage growth factor. It favours central symmetric zones while sparing apices and costophrenic angles. Patients pick up Nocardia infections, and whole lung lavage remains the defining treatment.

steps.title: The CRAZY causes list
steps.tx: **Crazy paving causes** span infection, oedema, haemorrhage, malignancy and proteinosis. Pneumocystis pneumonia in advanced HIV, viral pneumonia, cardiogenic oedema, diffuse alveolar haemorrhage and mucinous adenocarcinoma formerly called bronchioloalveolar carcinoma all stack septa over ground glass. Fever, immune state, heart size and speed of onset sort the list faster than any single density measurement on the scan.

steps.title: Lipoid pneumonia hides fat density
steps.tx: **Lipoid pneumonia** follows aspiration of mineral or vegetable oils, classically in older adults taking liquid paraffin for constipation. Its consolidation can join the crazy paving list, but the giveaway is fat density inside the opacity, measuring negative Hounsfield values where pneumonia should sit near soft tissue density. Fire eaters and children swallowing hydrocarbons get the acute form with chemical pneumonitis within hours.

steps.title: Ground glass in interstitial disease
steps.tx: **Nonspecific interstitial pneumonia** shows the pictured ground glass with traction bronchiectasis and immediate subpleural sparing, a combination that separates it from usual interstitial pneumonia. Usual interstitial pneumonia instead stacks subpleural honeycombing at the bases with almost no ground glass. The ground glass here signals inflammatory, steroid responsive change, while honeycombing signals fixed fibrosis that will not reverse with treatment.

steps.title: Anterior mediastinal masses: the four Ts
steps.tx: **Anterior mediastinal compartment** holds thymus, thyroid extensions, lymph nodes and the heart border, and its mass list is taught as the four Ts: thymoma, teratoma, thyroid and terrible lymphoma. A mass erasing the heart border silhouette sits in this compartment. Thymoma pairs with myasthenia gravis, teratoma can show fat, fluid, soft tissue and calcification in one mass, and lymphoma wraps vessels without narrowing them.

steps.title: Middle and posterior mediastinum
steps.tx: **Middle mediastinal compartment** contains nodes, trachea, oesophagus and great vessels, so its masses are mostly lymphadenopathy, foregut duplication cysts and vascular rings. The posterior compartment hugs the spine and grows neurogenic tumours, meningoceles and descending aortic aneurysms. A posterior mass that widens the neural foramen on CT is a nerve sheath tumour until proven otherwise, and it changes the surgical approach completely.

steps.title: Localising by silhouette and lines
steps.tx: **Mediastinal lines** on the frontal film place a mass before CT. Loss of the heart border silhouette means anterior, loss of the paravertebral line means posterior, and a mass seen through the heart shadow with borders intact sits in the posterior inferior compartment. The cervicothoracic sign adds the clavicle rule: a top border surviving above the clavicles cannot be anterior, pointing instead to neck or posterior origin.
steps.say: Mediastinal lines on the frontal film place a mass before CT. Loss of the heart border means anterior, loss of the paravertebral line means posterior, and a mass seen through the heart with borders intact sits posteriorly. A top border surviving above the clavicles cannot be anterior either.
